title: Global mate square for explicit affine tensor coordinates
statement: Let R,A,R',A' be commutative rings with R-algebra structures on A,R' and a structure map A tensor_R R' to A'. Let phi_g':A to A' and phi_f':R' to A' be its restrictions and assume their spectrum square is cartesian. Let M be an A-K-flat unbounded complex, K a quasi-coherent derived object on Spec A, e:Q(tilde M) isomorphic to K, L=Lg'^*K quasi-coherent and its counit on tilde M invertible. For any tensor cohomology model m and integer i, use the explicit U and a of [def-pc-affine-base-change-tilde-coordinates] with canonical target coordinate b. There exist a natural affine direct-image cohomology presentation d:Gamma H^i(-), restricted to R' and associated sheaf, isomorphic to H^i(Rf'_*(-)), and eU:tilde(restrict_R' U) isomorphic to H^i(Lg^*Rf_*K), with eU.hom followed by cohomology of the canonical base-change mate equal to tilde(restrict_R' a) followed by d at L. No stalk or localization conclusion is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8 affine proof and equation-bc; Tags 06Y6, 08IB, 01I9 and 01HV

proof.text: Apply the canonical affine comparison to baseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A R' M A', obtaining d and e0 and its square. Apply localized model independence to the supplied m and the fixed model to obtain a D-module source isomorphism s commuting with their localized comparison maps.

Set eU to F.mapIso(s) followed by e0. Functoriality of F and associativity transport the fixed-model square. Unfold the explicit module arrow; the localized comparison equation proves s.hom followed by the fixed arrow equals the supplied arrow. This gives exactly the original natural d and square.
